description: Docs-family handoff contract (spec / plan review + fix rounds; the docs-family shell + return constants live in template-contract.json#sections). Doc identity is doc_path + doc_hash; write findings, not status — the engine derives status from findings (review) or trusts the declared status (fix). Each property below documents its rule. Breaking change (engine major): the docs handoff carries the same lifecycle contract core as the task family — status gains TIMEOUT and commits{base,head} lands (the reverse of the legacy 'Docs rounds carry no commits field' declaration); docs consumers that relied on the commits-free docs handoff must migrate to the unified core.

phase.description: dispatch phase (review / fix); determined by the engine, not authored.

status.description: The round conclusion (this dispatch's terminal result) — APPROVED: done; CHANGES_REQUESTED: fix the findings (terminal conclusion of a review round; the fix loop runs as its own dispatch); REVIEW_FIX: the warn/nit-only review conclusion (收口态 — the review closed and its fix round routes the task to complete without a re-review, #278); BLOCKED: the round cannot proceed — the failure mechanism lives in failure_category, the reason in blocker; TIMEOUT: budget or liveness exceeded (engine-written attribution; the docs channel declares the same status enum as the task family). Orthogonal surfaces: failure_category (mechanism channel) and unverifiable[]/plan_conflicts[] (content-level notes) never fold into status. Review may omit this field — the engine derives it from findings; fix (work type) declares it and the engine passes it through. Write findings, not status.

failure_category.description: Failure mechanism channel — which mechanism ended the round (TIMEOUT / CONTRACT_VIOLATION / ENGINE_SELF_WRITTEN / EXECUTION_FAILURE / UNVERIFIABLE / PLAN_CONFLICT). Orthogonal to status (the round conclusion) and to the content-level unverifiable[]/plan_conflicts[] notes. Engine-written on failure paths. A BLOCKED round may satisfy its grounding via this field (see allOf).

commits.description: commit identity of the dispatch's review/fix range; the template-contract review range check at 13.5 validates it.

base.description: range base (TASK_BASE / FIXED_POINT): full 40-char SHA; never --short / %h / any truncated form.

head.description: full 40-char SHA; never --short / %h / any truncated form. Optional — omitted when the round has no head yet (e.g. some BLOCKED branch-review payloads).

doc_path.description: the reviewed document's exact path — must match the doc argument, do not rewrite relative forms.

doc_hash.description: content state token (sha256 of the doc at review time); legacy handoffs may omit it.

findings.description: [{lens, severity, section|file, line?, summary, fix}] — every review finding; severity blocker → CHANGES_REQUESTED, warn/nit → REVIEW_FIX (review rolls up; fix keeps declared findings, #278).

file.description: repo-relative path of a file this round changed.

reason.description: why the file changed (finding id / fix intent); omitted entries stay attributed by file.

changes.description: Changed-file attribution ledger (fix rounds declare every file the round touched, each with its reason). The engine reconciles `git diff <base>..HEAD` against it — files off the ledger are surfaced (warn + notes), never blocked; the review scope axis judges them as findings. The docs commitment boundary is the same as the task family (commits{base,head}), not doc_path alone.

artifacts.description: point at files, do not embed report bodies — values are paths (e.g. {"doc": "<path>"}), never inline content.

round.description: review/fix round number (engine-derived; canonical naming embeds it in the filename).

unverifiable.description: Content-level notes — each entry states one claim the round could not verify (what + why: e.g. {claim, why}). A non-empty list makes the round BLOCKED with failure_category UNVERIFIABLE and a blocker summarizing the entries. Dev-measured acceptance items (plan-constraints §口径) are NOT unverifiable: an evidence-contract accepted-noted round records them in `notes`, never writes unverifiable and never blocks.

plan_conflicts.description: Content-level notes — each entry states one plan conflict discovered during the round. A non-empty list makes the round BLOCKED with failure_category PLAN_CONFLICT and a blocker summarizing the entries.

blocker.description: The round's single real blocker line — states what could not be verified and why, or the concrete reason the round cannot proceed. Real sources only (agent-declared / engine gate reason / failure mechanism / unverifiable summary); never fabricated. Omit when nothing blocks (NOT null) — null is invalid. BLOCKED requires a non-empty blocker or a failure_category (see allOf).
